meta.title: Password reset by email link
meta.description: A forgotten password reset with a single-use emailed link: the request, the email, the link and the new password, in call order.

summary.headline: The link carries a random single-use token; only its hash is stored, it expires in 30 minutes and using it signs the account out everywhere.
points: The first answer is the same whether or not the email has an account
Only a SHA-256 hash of the token is stored, so a database leak cannot reset passwords
The token is consumed when the new password is saved, so the link works once
All sessions are revoked and the user is told by email that the password changed

data.title: User
data.subtitle: Browser and inbox
data.description: A patient who has forgotten the password to the Brightwater Health portal.

data.title: Account service
data.subtitle: Brightwater Health portal
data.description: Issues and checks reset tokens, hashes the new password and revokes existing sessions.

data.title: User database
data.subtitle: Accounts and sessions
data.description: Holds the account, the password hash and the session records that are revoked after a reset.

data.title: Token store
data.subtitle: Reset token hashes
data.description: Keeps the hash of each reset token with the account id. The key expires on its own after 30 minutes.

data.title: Email provider
data.subtitle: Transactional email API
data.description: Sends the reset link and the password-changed notice from a domain with SPF, DKIM and DMARC set up.

steps.title: Overview
steps.description: A patient cannot sign in to the Brightwater Health portal and asks for a reset link. Four moments matter: the request, the email, the link and the new password.

steps.title: The user asks for a reset
steps.description: The account service finds the account, creates 32 random bytes as the token and stores only their SHA-256 hash with a 30-minute expiry. The answer is the same for unknown addresses, so the form cannot be used to find accounts.

steps.title: The link is emailed
steps.description: The service queues the email with the raw token in the link. The provider delivers it; the token itself is never stored or logged on Brightwater's side.

steps.title: The user opens the link
steps.description: The service hashes the token from the URL and looks it up. A missing or expired hash shows a 'link expired' page; a match shows the new password form.

steps.title: The new password is saved
steps.description: On submit the service checks the token again and deletes it, so the link cannot be used twice. It saves the Argon2id hash of the new password and revokes every existing session.

steps.title: The user is told
steps.description: A second email confirms the change and says what to do if it was not them. The user signs in again with the new password.
